The above appeal is filed by the insured-owner of the vehicle challenging the judgment and award dated 2.5.2013 passed in MVC No.30/2010 by the Senior Civil Judge, Member, Additional MACT.,

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. The relevant facts necessary for consideration of the present appeal are that claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.12.2008, the 1st Respondent claimant filed a claim Hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' NC: 2024:KHC:2272 petition before the Tribunal arraying the owner and insurer of the offending bus as Respondent Nos.1 and 3 respectively before the Tribunal.
The driver was arrayed as Respondent No.2 before the Tribunal and the petition against him was dismissed.
The insurer contested the claim proceedings by filing statement of objections and took a specific contention that the driver of the bus did not have a licence to drive the insured vehicle.
4. The claimant examined himself as PW.1.
Exhibits P1 to P10 were marked in evidence.
No oral or documentary evidence has been adduced by the Respondents.

The Tribunal by its judgment and award dated 02.05.2013 partly allowed the claim petition and ordered a compensation of `35,691/-
together with interest @ 6% per annum and directed the owner of the vehicle to pay the compensation awarded and exonerated the insurer from the payment of compensation.

Being M/S Durgamba Motors vs Sri M K Murthy on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30946284/
2 aggrieved the present appeal is filed by the owner.

sentences.text: 5. Along with the above appeal, I.A.2/2014 is filed under Order 41 Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to NC: 2024:KHC:2272 permit the appellant to produce the additional evidence.
Along with the said application, a copy of driving licence extract is produced.

6. Learned counsel for the Appellant in support of the appeal and the application submits that the Tribunal while appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record has noticed that there is a difference in the name of the driver.

Further, it has appreciated the evidence of RW1 - RTO who has stated the driver Sri N.Dwaraka had no licence to drive the bus and that the Petitioner has not taken steps to produce the badge, has exonerated the insurer from the payment of compensation.

He further submits that document produced along with I.A.2/2014 has also marked as Ex.R1, clearly discloses that the driver was duly authorized to drive heavy transport vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Hence, he seeks for allowing of the above appeal and holding that the insurer is liable to pay the compensation awarded.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for Respondent No.3 - insurer justifies the award of the Tribunal and seeks for dismissal of the above appeal and the application.
The submissions of both the learned counsels have been considered and the material on record have been perused including the records of the Tribunal.
The question that arise for consideration is 'Whether the finding of the Tribunal with regard to exonerating the liability on the insurer is erroneous and liable to be interfered with?'.
It is forthcoming the document produced along with I.A.2/2014 is marked as Ex.P1.
Hence, consideration of I.A.2/2014 is unnecessary for the purpose of adjudication of its appeal.
Hence, I.A.2/ is dismissed .
9. The date of the accident is 09.12.2008.
It is forthcoming from FIR - Ex.P1 that the name of the driver is Dwaraka N. S/o. Narayana Swamy.
In the driving licence (Ex.R1) the name of the driver shown as Dwaraka S/o. Narasimha Murthy.
There is no much dispute with regard to the identity of the driver who was driving the vehicle.

10. It is further forthcoming from the extract of the driving licence (Ex.R1) that the driver was authorized to drive the heavy transport vehicle and which licence was valid from 11.08.2006 to 10.08.2009.
Although the NC: 2024:KHC:2272 Tribunal noticed the driving licence (Ex.R1)
, the contents of the same have not been noticed for the purpose of appreciating the matter that is required to be adjudicated i.e., with regard to the driving licence.
11. It is forthcoming from the material on record that the driver of the vehicle was duly licenced to drive the vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Hence, the finding of the Tribunal regarding liability being erroneous, the same is liable to be interfered with in the present appeal.

Hence, the question M/S Durgamba Motors vs Sri M K Murthy on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30946284/
3 framed for consideration is answered in the affirmative.
